citations.narrative:
The west facing windows of the tropical building have an irregular green, black, and a brownish film coating the windows,
ceiling and supporting framework that is consistent with algae, mold or mildew. Keepers stated that work orders to clean
the windows had been submitted multiple times only to be removed without completing the work. Ensuring primary
enclosures are kept clean and in good repair helps protect the birds from injury and disease. Primary enclosures must be
constructed and maintained so that they ensure that all surfaces in contact with the birds may be readily cleaned and/or
sanitized in accordance with 3.158 or be replaced when worn or soiled.
Correct by October 23, 2026
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representatives.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
